We can perform any number of operations. Each operation costs x and rotates the types: after operation, the chocolate originally at index i (i.e., type i before operation?) becomes type ((i+1) mod n) for all chocolates simultaneously. Actually we need to think about the effect on the array of costs.

Interpretation: each position i initially has a chocolate of type i, with cost nums[i] to collect. We can decide to collect a chocolate at any time, after any number of operations (including zero) before collecting. After performing k operations, the chocolate that originally was at position i will have type (i + k) mod n. Conversely, at a given time after k operations, the chocolate of type t is located at position (t - k) mod n (since we want the position i such that (i + k) mod n = t => i = (t - k) mod n). So if we have performed k operations, then to collect a chocolate of type t we would need to collect it from position (t - k) mod n, paying cost nums[(t - k) mod n].

We can collect each type at most once? We need to collect chocolates of all types (i.e., at least one chocolate of each type). We can collect multiple chocolates (maybe same type multiple times) but we need at least one of each type. Since collecting a chocolate incurs its cost (the nums value at its current position) and we can collect as many as we want, obviously we would not collect extra chocolates beyond needed because costs are positive. So we need to collect exactly one chocolate of each type, each possibly after a different number of operations (i.e., we can collect some types before some operations, others after more operations).
